result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.add_hypercube_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a d-dimensional hypercube graph Q(d) to the current graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L7756-L7851){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_hypercube_graph( d, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Hypercube graph](/assets/graphs/add-hypercube-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three hypercube graphs side by side for d=1, 2, and 3: a single edge, a square, and a cube drawn in perspective. Each dimension doubles the graph, joining every node to its copy, so the d-cube has 2^d nodes and every node has d neighbors." width="100%"} The hypercube has one node for every string of `d` bits, and two nodes are joined when their strings differ in exactly one bit. It has `2^d` nodes and `d * 2^(d - 1)` edges, every node has degree `d`, and the shortest-path distance between two nodes is the number of bits in which they differ (their Hamming distance), so the diameter is `d`. `Q(1)` is a single edge, `Q(2)` a square, and `Q(3)` the cube. Each node is labelled with its bit string (e.g. `"0110"`), and nodes are created in binary counting order, from `"00...0"` to `"11...1"`. In a directed graph every edge points from the string with a `0` to the one with a `1` in the differing bit. The hypercube is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Hypercubes are useful for: - modeling interconnection networks for parallel computers and distributed hash tables, where each node links to the nodes one bit-flip away - state spaces of `d` on/off switches, where an edge is a single flip (e.g. Boolean network or genotype spaces) - test cases for highly symmetric, bipartite, regular graphs with known distances ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [d]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dimension (number of bits). Must be at least `1`. The node count doubles with each dimension, so `d=20` already gives about a million nodes. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each node is labelled with its bit string. Because these labels don't depend on the existing nodes, adding a second labelled hypercube of the same dimension raises `ValueError` (labels are unique); pass `label=False` for the second one. If `False`, nodes are created without labels. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `d=` is less than `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The cube `Q(3)` has `8` nodes, `12` edges, and diameter `3`: ::: {#cfc118be .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_hypercube_graph(d=3) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges(), graph.get_diameter() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (8, 12, 3) ``` ::: ::: The labels are bit strings, and each node's neighbors are the strings one bit-flip away: ::: {#33b4e2c9 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} sorted(graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.neighbors("000")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['001', '010', '100'] ``` ::: ::: The distance between two nodes is the number of bits that differ: ::: {#7378ed91 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.shortest_path_length("001", "110") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 3 ``` ::: :::
